lessons.title: Why we prune and the tools we use
lessons.html:
Why we prune macadamia trees

Pruning means cutting away some branches of a tree. We do it for a reason. A good cut helps the tree. A bad cut can hurt the tree for many years.

On a macadamia farm we prune to:

  • Shape young trees. A young tree needs one strong main stem, called the central leader. Strong side branches grow out from it.
  • Let in light and air. A thick, dark tree carries fewer nuts inside. Light and air also help to keep diseases away.
  • Lift the skirt. Low branches touching the ground get in the way when nuts fall and are picked up. We cut them so the ground under the tree stays open.
  • Keep the rows open. Tractors, sprayers and bakkies must be able to drive between the rows.
  • Remove dead, broken and sick wood. This wood can carry pests and disease.

The tools

ToolUse it for
SecateursThin shoots, up to about the thickness of your finger
LoppersThicker branches you can reach from the ground
Pruning sawBig branches
Pole prunerHigh branches, so you do not climb

Look after your tools

  • Keep blades sharp. A blunt blade tears the bark.
  • Clean blades when you move to a new block, as your supervisor tells you. Dirty blades can carry disease from tree to tree.
  • Put tools back in the store at the end of the day.

Stay safe

  • Wear gloves, safety glasses and closed shoes.
  • Never point a saw or blade towards your body.
  • Only trained and authorised workers may use a chainsaw.
  • Use a ladder only if you have been shown how, and only on firm, flat ground. Never stand on the top step.

lessons.title: Making good cuts and cleaning up
lessons.html:
How to prune a macadamia tree

Your supervisor will tell you which block to prune and what kind of pruning to do. Always listen to the instructions for that block. Pruning is usually done after the harvest is finished.

Steps

  1. Walk around the tree first. Look at it from all sides.
  2. Find dead, broken and sick branches. Cut these out first.
  3. Find branches that cross and rub against each other. Remove the weaker one.
  4. Cut low branches that hang near the ground, to the height your supervisor gives you.
  5. On young trees, keep one central leader. If two stems compete at the top, remove the weaker one.
  6. Thin the inside of the tree a little so light can get in. Do not take too much. A tree that loses too many leaves will carry fewer nuts.

A good cut

  • Cut close to the branch collar. The collar is the small swollen ring where a branch joins a bigger branch or the stem.
  • Do not leave a long stump. Stumps rot and let in disease.
  • Do not cut into the collar or flush against the stem. The tree heals from the collar.
  • For a heavy branch, make three cuts: a small cut underneath, then a cut on top further out to drop the weight, then the final cut at the collar. This stops the bark from tearing down the stem.

Clean up

  • Pull cut branches into the middle of the row, or where your supervisor says, so they can be chipped or removed.
  • Do not leave branches under the trees. They get in the way at harvest time.
  • Tell your supervisor about any tree that looks sick, has borer holes or has split bark.

Key points

  • Prune to shape young trees, let in light and keep the ground under trees open.
  • Remove dead, broken, sick and crossing branches first.
  • Cut at the branch collar and never leave a stump.
  • Use three cuts for heavy branches.
  • Keep tools sharp and clean, and wear your safety gear.

quiz.question: What is the central leader of a young macadamia tree?

options.text: The lowest branch near the ground
The one strong main stem of the tree
The worker who leads the pruning team
A thin shoot growing from the roots

quiz.question: Which tool should you use for a thin shoot about the thickness of your finger?

options.text: Pruning saw
Pole pruner
Chainsaw
Secateurs

quiz.question: Which branches should you cut out first?

options.text: Dead, broken and sick branches
The healthiest branches at the top
Any branch carrying nuts
Branches on the north side only

quiz.question: Where should you make the final cut when removing a branch?

options.text: In the middle of the branch, leaving a stump
Deep into the main stem
Close to the branch collar, without cutting into it
Anywhere, as long as the branch falls

quiz.question: Why do we cut low branches that hang near the ground?

options.text: To make the tree grow taller faster
To keep the ground under the tree open for nuts to be picked up
Because low branches never carry nuts
To feed the branches to cattle

options.text: True
False

quiz.question: Cutting too many leaves from a tree can mean it carries fewer nuts.

options.text: True
False

quiz.question: Which of these are good pruning practices? (select all that apply)

options.text: Keep blades sharp so they do not tear the bark
Leave cut branches lying under the trees
Use three cuts to remove a heavy branch
